reason: The collagen messages and amino acid supply suggest making collagen proteins next.

effect: The muscle-forming cells are prepared; the remaining goal is to make living supporting tissue.
reaction: The contrast between retained muscle proteins and exported collagen clarifies their different roles.
reason: Living fibroblasts and their collagen-rich matrix are the two components needed for the supporting tissue.
expectation: The fibroblasts and matrix should form a living supporting tissue.

effect: Combining the fibroblasts with their matrix completed the supporting tissue and the chapter, clarifying that the tissue includes both living cells and extracellular material.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the separately constructed cells and matrix come together.

mostWorthwhile.text: The parallel uses of amino acids were most worthwhile: the illustration plans connect different RNA messages to exported collagen in fibroblasts and retained muscle proteins in myoblasts.

leastWorthwhile.text: The muscle precursor result repeats much of its picture description in two passages. The lineage terms, especially paraxial mesoderm and myoblasts, could also use brief explanations for readers new to anatomy.

surprise.text: The matrix alone did not complete the supporting-tissue goal; it needed to be brought together with the living fibroblasts. That emphasized the tissue's cellular and extracellular components.

arbitrary.text: The final combination felt slightly artificial because the matrix picture already placed living fibroblasts beside it, although explicitly assembling tissue had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: the unfinished muscle branch makes me curious how separate myoblasts become mature fibres, and the contrasting protein destinations made this chapter informative.
